math_plain: Simulating jiggly volumetric materials at multiple detail levels simultaneously: coarse motion captures bulk deformation, while high-frequency detail is split and recombined with finer resolutions to add bouncy wrinkles without multiplying the number of time-steps needed.

math_plain: The system learns to recognize face identity in stylized portraits by matching human perception: it observes human same-different judgments on diverse art styles and trains encoders to rank face similarities the same way humans do, learning which features truly signal the same person.

math_plain: A porous material's internal structure is designed so its effective mechanical properties (how it bends and stretches as a whole) are uniform in all directions, while its visual appearance halftones a target image. Balancing visual appearance against uniform stiffness is the core constraint.

math_plain: High-resolution shape-optimization problems are solved by building Newton's method atop a block-accelerated sparse linear solver that exploits the fact that unknowns cluster naturally into dense d-by-d blocks. This structure speeds up every phase: assembly, factorization, and back-solve.

math_plain: 3D spatial data (meshes, volumes, light fields) is compressed by recognizing that many regions are similar up to a geometric transformation; store only one copy of each unique piece plus the transformations between copies, using octree subdivision and rotation groups for compactness.

math_plain: A diffusion model for 3D shapes is fine-tuned efficiently by recognizing the natural temporal structure of detail-generation in flow-based models: learn coarse structure first, then details, and combine predictions from multiple viewing angles to resolve the ambiguity that single views introduce.

math_plain: Text-guided image editing in diffusion transformers works by discovering which attention heads respond to which visual semantics, then routing text tokens selectively to the heads that control the regions you want to edit. The system learns head sensitivity without retraining.

math_plain: A pretrained 3D generative model encodes an object and predicts colored labels on its reconstructed surface; these colors act as part indicators. The system learns part segmentation by repurposing the model's internal structure knowledge without annotated training data for the segmentation task itself.

math_plain: Light bouncing many times through dense hair is expensive to track; instead, treat the hair as a participating medium that scatters light, and stochastically sample one scattering event to approximate higher-order bounces while using explicit fiber geometry for direct lighting detail.

math_plain: Recovering material and lighting from images is a high-variance, brittle optimization problem; a spatial blending field interpolates locally between cached radiance estimates and standard unbiased samplers, reducing variance while keeping gradients well-behaved for reliable parameter recovery.
